REGARDING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's aspirations, so that every child has the right to survival, to grow and develop, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.
Likewise women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and quality. Through the role of women and families, society and the state will produce resilient generations who will continue the nation's aspirations.
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Katingan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to provide protection for Women and Children victims of violence so that it needs to be regulated in Regional Regulations.
So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the regions so that institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, implementation, handling, empowerment, guidance and supervision of the protection of women in Katingan Regency.

Article 8
(1) The community may participate and be responsible in the service, prevention, assistance, recovery and monitoring of victims of violence.
(2) Community participation and responsibility as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in the form of:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children; b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against Women and Children to the competent authorities;
c. providing emergency assistance; and
d. providing protection to victims of violence.

CHAPTER VI
MINIMUM SERVICE STANDARDS
Article 10
(1) MSS is implemented by the Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children with the aim of ensuring that Women and Children victims of violence receive the minimum services needed.
(2) MSS as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services: a. handling of complaints/reports of victims of violence against women and children;
b. health rehabilitation for women and children victims of violence; c. social rehabilitation for women and children victims of violence; d. legal assistance for women and children victims of violence; e. recovery/psychological services for women and children victims of violence; f. mediation for women and children victims of violence; and
g. repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.

Article 3
Protection of Women and Children victims of violence aims to:
a. prevent all forms of violence against women and children; b. protect women and children as well as provide services to women and Children victims of violence; and
c. empower women and Children victims of violence.

Article 9
Paragraph (1) Sufficiently Clear.
- 12 - Paragraph (2) Point a Sufficiently Clear.
Point b What is meant by "health rehabilitation" is action provided to restore the physical, psychological, and social functions of victims as a result of the violence they experienced in order to restore bodily functions that are experiencing problems.
Point c What is meant by "social rehabilitation" is the process of restoring functions and development that enables victims to carry out their social functions properly in community life.
Point d What is meant by "legal aid" is the guarantee of legal protection and guarantee of equality before the law for victims.
Point e Sufficiently Clear.
Point f Sufficiently Clear.
Point g What is meant by "repatriation" is the effort to return victims of violence to their region of origin.
What is meant by "social reintegration" is the guidance effort carried out to provide opportunities for the community and victims of violence to be able to interact and socialize with each other to eliminate existing negative stigma.
Paragraph (3) Sufficiently Clear.

Article 6
Child victims of violence, in addition to obtaining the rights as referred to in Article 5, also obtain special rights as follows:
a. respect for survival, growth and development; b. to education, health and access to parents during the handling process; and
c. to obtain equal protection related to status, citizenship, race, skin color, gender, language, religion, politics, disability, birth or other status.

1.5.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, the definition of “Kekerasan” (Pasal 1 angka 8) includes “penelantaran” (neglect) alongside physical/sexual/psychological violence, threats, coercion, and arbitrary deprivation of liberty. However, the regulation does not explicitly mention “kekerasan ekonomi” (economic violence) or economic deprivation/financial control as a form of violence. The judge inferred economic violence from the mere citation of UU 23/2004 (PKDRT) in the preamble, but that is not an explicit inclusion of economic violence in this Perda’s scope. Since the retrieved passages did not contain explicit economic-violence language, a correct decision should have been No; the judge’s reasoning was overly inferential.

6. Woman is an adult human of female gender and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a Child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public and or in private life.

2.2.rationale: The original Indonesian text mentions community participation (Pasal 15) and lists actors including “lembaga swadaya masyarakat” (NGOs), “swasta,” etc., and also allows the government to utilize shelters owned by the community/other social service institutions (Pasal 12 ayat (3)). But these provisions describe participation/support in general terms; they do not establish a concrete institutional collaboration mechanism (e.g., formal partnerships, contracting, accreditation, MoUs, defined roles in service delivery) with non-government service providers. The judge treated the mere mention of NGOs/community actors as proof of an institutional collaboration mechanism, which is too lenient given the indicator. The English candidates accurately reflect the Indonesian, so the error is the judge’s interpretation.

4.1.rationale: In the Indonesian text, Pasal 15(1)(c) states the community may “melakukan sosialisasi hak Perempuan dan Anak secara mandiri” (independently socialize/disseminate information about women’s and children’s rights). This is a general community role and is not framed as a government-led prevention program providing structured information/education specifically on violence against women (VAW). The regulation’s prevention language is broad (e.g., Pasal 3(a) ‘mencegah segala bentuk kekerasan’ and Pasal 8(2)(a) ‘mencegah terjadinya tindak kekerasan’), but it does not set out an explicit information/education intervention on VAW. The judge equated general “socialization of rights” with an information/education program on VAW, which over-extends what the text says; thus the failure is in evaluation/thresholding, not translation or retrieval.

Letter h What is meant by "legal certainty" is the existence of legal norms that do not conflict with other regulations and provide legal security for victims of violence from the arbitrariness of certain parties.

4.2.rationale: The Indonesian regulation includes “keadilan dan kesetaraan gender” as a principle (Pasal 2 huruf b) and explains “kesetaraan gender” in the elucidation, but it does not mandate or describe education/curricula/training to promote gender equality. Pasal 15(1)(c) only mentions general “sosialisasi hak Perempuan dan Anak” (rights socialization), which is not the same as gender-equality education. The judge inferred that rights socialization ‘constitutes’ gender equality education, but the text does not explicitly provide such an education measure. The English candidates reflect the Indonesian accurately; the mislabel comes from the judge being too permissive.
